question: For $f(x)=kx-x^3$, determine the values of $k$ for which $f'(x)<0$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Hence state the monotonic behaviour of the function.
explanation:
Given function
$$f(x)=kx-x^3$$
First derivative
$$f'(x)=k-3x^2$$
Necessary condition
For $f'(x)<0$ for every real $x$, the condition must also hold at $x=0$. Therefore,
$$f'(0)=k<0$$
Sufficiency of the condition
If $k<0$, then $-3x^2\leq0$, and consequently,
$$k-3x^2\leq k<0$$
for every real $x$. Thus, the condition is sufficient as well as necessary.
Conclusion
The required range is $k<0$. For these values of $k$, the function is strictly decreasing on $\mathbb{R}$.

options.A: $k\leq0$; the function is strictly decreasing on $\mathbb{R}$
options.B: $k>0$; the function is strictly decreasing on $\mathbb{R}$
options.C: $k<0$; the function is strictly decreasing on $\mathbb{R}$
options.D: $k=0$ only; the function is strictly decreasing on $\mathbb{R}$
